title: iandunn.net full redesign
intro: My picks are already selected. Change only the ones you disagree with, add notes where I ask for facts, then send.

decisions.question: What should the site lead with, and what is the one thing a visitor should do?
decisions.context: Today the hero is a leadership aphorism with a Pinterest title line. Every page points somewhere different.

options.label: Person first, products as proof
options.detail: An engineering leader who actually ships things. Main action: email or book a call.
options.why: Your strongest material is the combination — the career line plus four real shipped products. Neither alone is as interesting.

options.label: Products first
options.detail: A maker's storefront: FutAve and TheraBasics lead, the person is the footnote. Main action: visit the products.

options.label: Writing first
options.detail: A notebook that happens to have an author page. Honest only if you plan to publish regularly.

decisions.question: FutAve — what is true today?
decisions.context: The site says Live, with App Store and Play links (all answer 200). But futave.com now says "Find your next match" — the wave-detector framing in your copy no longer matches the product's own positioning.

options.label: Keep, refresh the copy
options.detail: Status Live stays; the write-up gets rewritten to the product's current positioning.
options.why: The product is clearly alive; only the story about it has drifted.

options.label: Keep exactly as written
options.detail: Wave Detector framing stays even though futave.com no longer leads with it.

options.label: Something bigger changed
options.detail: Tell me in a note what moved (domain, stores, status).

decisions.question: TheraBasics — what is true today?
decisions.context: The site says Live with both store links; therabasics.com answers and is on-message (individuals, therapists, and coaches).

options.label: Keep as Live
options.detail: Status and links stay; copy still gets the general refresh.
options.why: Site and both store listings respond, and the positioning matches your write-up.

options.label: Status changed
options.detail: Tell me in a note what it is now.

options.label: Drop it from the site
options.detail: It disappears from the portfolio entirely.

decisions.question: Center Ref — what is true today?
decisions.context: The site says Public beta, no store links. centerref.com is up and on-message. I cannot tell from outside whether it shipped, stalled, or stopped. Not checked.

options.label: Still public beta
options.detail: Keeps the current status.
options.why: Matches what centerref.com itself still says; correct me in a note if it shipped or stopped.

options.label: Now live
options.detail: Status flips to Live; add store or TestFlight links in a note if any.

options.label: Abandoned — drop it
options.detail: It disappears from the portfolio.

decisions.question: Stonefold — keep or cut?
decisions.context: Listed as Prototype with "nothing to show yet": no link, no screenshot. You said some projects are abandoned; this is the likeliest candidate.

options.label: Cut it
options.detail: Three real products make a stronger page than three products and an empty promise. It can return when there is something to show.
options.why: An entry with no artifact weakens the page it sits on, and cutting is free to reverse.

options.label: Keep as prototype
options.detail: Stays as a fourth entry, still with nothing to show.

options.label: Keep as a one-line mention
options.detail: Not a full entry — a single line in the projects page's closing text.

decisions.question: How many pages should the new site have?
decisions.context: Today: Home, About, Case studies, Writing, Contact. The Contact page is six cards restating links the footer already has.

options.label: Four — fold Contact away
options.detail: Home, About, Projects, Writing. Contact becomes a proper footer and a line in the hero.
options.why: The contact page duplicates the footer; every channel survives, one template-smelling page disappears.

options.detail: Contact stays its own page, redesigned.

decisions.question: What happens to Writing?
decisions.context: Today it is four category cards and an archive frame around exactly one post (July 2026).

options.label: Keep, as a plain list
options.detail: The category cards and archive framing go; a simple dated list of posts stays, currently one entry.
options.why: Honest at any post count, and the one post you have is good.

options.label: Cut until there are three posts
options.detail: The section and nav item disappear for now; the post keeps its URL.

options.label: Keep the full structure
options.detail: Categories and archive stay, promising a cadence that does not exist yet.

decisions.question: Where does the parish / board / AYSO section live?
decisions.context: "The other half of the week" — vestry, Good Shepherd Manor board, Sunday livestream, Saturday refereeing — currently sits on the home page.

options.label: On About
options.detail: Home gets tighter; the section becomes part of the long-form story where a reader already has context.
options.why: It is the most human content on the site, but it answers "who is this person", which is the About page's question.

options.label: Stay on Home
options.detail: Keeps the humanizing note up front at the cost of a longer home page.

options.label: Drop it
options.detail: The site goes strictly professional.

decisions.question: How far does the copy refresh go?
decisions.context: Every project is written to the same visible template: opinion quote, "the problem that mattered", "the tradeoff I made", "why it's different".

options.label: Rewrite out of the formula
options.detail: Keep the facts and the good lines; each project gets its own shape and length. The about story keeps its substance.
options.why: The repeated scaffold is itself one of the AI tells; the underlying material is good and survives.

options.label: Light touch only
options.detail: Copy moves almost verbatim into the new design, formula and all.

decisions.question: How does the redesign reach the live site?
decisions.context: iandunn.net deploys from main to Cloudflare Pages. The build will take several phases; this choice is about what visitors see in between.

options.label: One release at the end
options.detail: Phases merge into a long-lived redesign branch; main gets one final merge. Visitors never see a half-redesigned site.
options.why: Old and new pages mixed live would look broken, and the site has no urgent content waiting.

options.label: Ship each phase to main
options.detail: The live site updates as each phase lands; faster feedback, mixed look for a week or two.

decisions.question: Who sets the new look's direction?
decisions.context: The installed taste-skill deals palette, type pairing, hero form and layout from randomized lists precisely so the result is not the model's habitual defaults. I can constrain the deal, or steer it to a lane first.

options.label: Trust the deal
options.detail: The dealer picks palette, type and hero form within hard constraints (below). Whatever it deals, we build well.
options.why: Escaping AI-default taste is the whole point; hand-steering reintroduces the defaults we are throwing away.

options.label: Quiet and personal lane
options.detail: Steer the deal toward light, photo-forward, understated — then let it pick within that.

options.label: Sharp and technical lane
options.detail: Steer toward engineer energy: mono accents, harder edges, possibly dark surfaces.

decided.what: This is a large job: three reviewers will read the plan once. Files live in docs/pare/full-redesign.
decided.why: A full-site redesign across several phases, landing on a live deployed site.

decided.what: The stack stays: Astro 5, static output, Cloudflare Pages, no adapter.
decided.why: The complaint is the look, not the machinery; the build pipeline works and costs nothing to keep.

decided.what: Kept assets: the seven portraits in public/photos. Product logos and app screenshots also stay available for whichever projects survive the fact-check.
decided.why: You named the photos as the keepers; logos and screenshots are facts about the products, not part of the discarded look.

decided.what: The build runs under the taste-skill (tasteskill 2.5) with its gate, with three hard constraints fed in: never violet (its own rule), no olive or sage (TheraBasics separation), and not cream-plus-terracotta again (the look being thrown away).
decided.why: You asked to install and use it; the constraints keep the deal from landing on either forbidden palette.

decided.what: A git tag marks the current state before the redesign lands, and CLAUDE.md's design-constraint section gets rewritten to describe the new system afterwards.
decided.why: v1-pre-redesign already exists as an earlier rollback point; the docs must describe the site that exists.

decided.what: No invented numbers, testimonials, or fake screenshots anywhere in the new site.
decided.why: Honest placeholders were already a rule here, and invented proof is the fastest way back to looking AI-made.
